synopsis: ISO 18497 covers automated agricultural machinery, including obstacle-detection testing, and the glossary identifies ISO 18497:2024 as the closest published cousin of the heavy off-road collision mitigation project's function [f15276, f15283]. The standard was revised in July 2024 into four parts covering design principles, obstacle protection systems, autonomous operating zones, and verification and validation; Chapter 12 specifically records publication of Parts 1, 2 and 4, replacing ISO 18497:2018 [f1393, f15284, f9763]. The corpus says ISO 18497 defines risk zones and physical test procedures but does not define how much testing may be virtual or prescribe virtual-evidence shares [f1953, f1249, f1954]. The glossary describes four detection failure categories—failure to detect, late detection, incorrect classification and localization error—reflecting the premise that no detection technology works perfectly in all conditions [f15285]. These substantive descriptions must be treated cautiously: Chapters 5, 10 and 13 say ISO 18497 details were not verified, and Chapter 5 recommends checking editions, application dates and simulation clauses before reliance [f4335, f7741, f11198].
